name: Koy Sanjaq Jewish Neo-Aramaic
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Mutzafi, Hezy. 2004. The Jewish Neo-Aramaic Dialect of Koy Sanjaq (Iraqi Kurdistan). Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. 278pp. (full grammar, includes phonology/stress; not freely online)

new_statements.quote: Unlike all other known NENA dialects, including the most archaizing among them, e.g. Qaraqosh, Alqosh and Ṭyare, where word stress is generally penultimate in nominal forms, Trans-Zab exhibits a shift of word stress from the penultimate to the ultimate syllable in the nominal system (with some exceptions, chiefly adverbs), most probably due to the influence of Kurdish and (in J.Az.) also of Azerbaijani. [p.411 fn.8:] Stress is penultimate unless otherwise indicated. [p.419:] ... the Trans-Zab dialect of Koy Sanjaq ...
new_statements.citation: Mutzafi, Hezy. 2008. "Trans-Zab Jewish Neo-Aramaic." Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 71(3): 409-431. doi 10.1017/S0041977X08000815
new_statements.locator: p. 415, section 4 'Penultimate > ultimate stress' (PDF page 7); transcription note p. 411 fn. 8 (PDF p. 3); J. Koy Sanjaq classed as Trans-Zab p. 419 (PDF p. 11) and abbreviation 'JKS = J. Koy Sanjaq' p. 410 fn. 1; JKS example nawtá 'nit' p. 416
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Trans-Zab Jewish NENA group, to which the Jewish dialect of Koy Sanjaq belongs, word stress in nominal forms (nouns, adjectives) falls on the final syllable, a shift from the pan-NENA penultimate pattern; adverbs are the chief exceptions. The paper's transcription default ('penultimate unless otherwise indicated') implies non-nominal words (verbs) keep penultimate stress, i.e. the placement is morphologically conditioned (nominal = final, verbal = penultimate), but the paper does not state the verbal rule for J. Koy Sanjaq explicitly.
new_statements.exceptions: 'with some exceptions, chiefly adverbs' (p.415); pretonic vowels in nominals remain long as a relic of the earlier penultimate stress (nāšá 'man', p.415).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level; the statement is a group-level (Trans-Zab) comparative-dialectological statement covering the nominal system only, made by the author of the Koy Sanjaq grammar from his own informant data; J. Koy Sanjaq forms are cited with final stress marks (nawtá 'nit'; ganāwá/ganaftá tables p.416 are Trans-Zab generic). The full grammar (Mutzafi 2004) presumably gives the dialect-specific rule including verbs and secondary stress and would supersede this.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1 koys1242 is named 'Koy Sanjaq Jewish Neo-Aramaic' but carries ISO 639-3 kqd, whose SIL reference name is 'Koy Sanjaq Surat' (Ethnologue's Christian Koy Sanjaq dialect); Wikipedia maps kqd/koys1242 to 'Koy Sanjaq Christian Neo-Aramaic' and gives koys1241 for the Jewish dialect, while Glottolog's koys1241 is a bare dialect node 'Koy Sanjaq'. The statement quoted here is for the JEWISH dialect of Koy Sanjaq (J. Koy Sanjaq / JKS, a Trans-Zab Jewish NENA dialect, Mutzafi 2004 grammar), matching Glottolog's name and sole descriptive reference for koys1242, not the Christian dialect (Mutzafi 2004 JAOS), which is not Trans-Zab and for which no stress statement was found.

sources.note: Sec. 4 'Penultimate > ultimate stress' (p.415): all NENA dialects have word stress 'generally penultimate in nominal forms' except Trans-Zab, which shifted nominal stress to the ultimate syllable 'with some exceptions, chiefly adverbs'; J. Koy Sanjaq (JKS) is explicitly a Trans-Zab dialect (p.410 fn.1, p.419) and JKS nominals are cited with final stress (nawtá 'nit', p.416); fn.8 p.411: 'Stress is penultimate unless otherwise indicated' (transcription default); p.429 lists the stress shift among early Trans-Zab areal features. Author's own informant data.
